test_groups.1: ARGINE_EXPERT_WAIT parsing (10 invalid spellings rejected) and fail-closed combinations (prefetch, read mode, retention policy)
test_groups.2: wait placement: after the first node, kind leaves exactly the up/down reads pending (mask = node kind) and their bytes are absent from memory until their own node; layer and layer_touch wait for all 9 reads at the first node
test_groups.3: one thread, budget pressure, 12 tokens x 4 layers: miss sequence (layer, expert, kind), eviction sequence, misses, bytes read, evictions and resident bytes identical in layer, layer_touch and kind, with both backends
test_groups.4: six threads: bytes correct at every node, no violation, no pending read, same misses and bytes without pressure
test_groups.5: a request needing space while up/down are in flight evicts only an older layer-1 slice; with no evictable slice it fails instead of evicting
test_groups.6: an all-hit layer waits for nothing
test_groups.7: an injected read error is reported at the node that waits for that read (kind: the down node; layer_touch: the first node)
test_groups.8: node order up, gate, down; only the last layer stays pinned; a kind unknown at the first node is issued and waited at its own node
test_groups.9: wait decisions and cache statistics identical with tracing on and off; a read completed in the background before its wait is counted hidden, with coherent I records
test_groups.10: independent-review cases: orphan reads counted and waited before pins are released; a later node with different experts is refused; synchronous completions never counted as background
test_groups.11: regression of the host heap-corruption incident: 48 short-lived threads with a per-thread object (created and destroyed once each, on live storage); 6 rounds of thread churn through the store and the trace (team threads of every arm plus reader threads with 8 reads in flight); per-thread runtime state created == destroyed; no read drained at thread exit; trace flushed; Windows: HeapValidate and _heapchk
